prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1434; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection, with the claimant represented by counsel from the outset. Assigned for investigation and contact made with the representative to request the initial statement and photographs.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the file. They confirm several details of the reported impact, although no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 3: Damage to the vehicle is mostly consistent with the impact described. A few old scratches are visible, and it is possible they predate this loss, so they are being noted separately for the estimate.

Entry 4: Confirmed that the driver lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 5: The claimant has described the event the same way in each conversation so far. It is not yet fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact, so this is being followed up with the representative.

Entry 6: Medical records report a shoulder injury, which is plausible for a crash of this type. No prior injury to the same area is known, and treatment has followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 7: Reviewed the file with the claim summary. Seating position remains the open item, and the evaluation will be updated once the representative responds to the outstanding request.
